how.title: Four steps from forgotten archive to a new beginning.

s1.title: Upload
s1.text: Add a PDF report, Markdown notes or a code folder tree, after your team agrees.

s2.title: Verify
s2.text: AI drafts the unfinished tasks. You keep, edit or remove each one before anything is public.

s3.title: Continue
s3.text: A team reads the teaser, then takes access right away or sends a short plan, as the owners chose.

s4.title: Continue with credit
s4.text: Each person who continues accepts the attribution agreement. Private files open and the lineage is logged.

g1.title: Every task cites its source
g1.text: Each drafted task links to a page or file, and ESTAFET checks that the quoted text really exists there.

g2.title: Nothing public until verified
g2.text: Publishing stays blocked until the owners have reviewed every drafted item.

g3.title: Team consent first
g3.text: Every team member has to confirm before the files are read by AI and before a project can be published.

wizard.effectPrivate: Your files, code and notes stay private.

terms.title: Terms and Conditions
terms.lead: ESTAFET helps student teams hand over discontinued competition and research projects to the next team. By using ESTAFET you agree to these terms.

s1.p: Anyone can browse projects without an account. To share a project or take access you need an account with a confirmed email. One account can both share and continue projects. You are responsible for keeping your password safe.

s2.p: You may share only a project you worked on and whose files you have the right to share. Every active team member must agree. Do not upload secrets (passwords, API keys), other people's personal data, or files you may not share. The public summary shows only what you reviewed and approved.

s3.p: Project files are not shown on public pages. Only the owners and people who hold access can open them. Owners choose whether access is open, by request, or paused.

s4.p: Anyone who takes access must accept the Attribution Agreement and credit the original owners in work built on it. Access can be revoked by the owners or the ESTAFET team with a written reason. The attribution duty stays after access is revoked.

s5.p: Anyone can report a project. The ESTAFET team can hold, hide or remove a project from public view based on the Community Guidelines. Every decision comes with a written reason, and owners can appeal once per decision. Moderation does not delete data, and agreements already accepted do not change.

s6.p: You can ask for an AI draft or fill everything in by hand. An AI draft is a suggestion: you review, edit or remove every item before publishing. You are responsible for what you publish.

s7.p: ESTAFET is a student project and is provided as is. We do not guarantee that the service is always available or error free, or that the content users share is accurate.

s8.p: If the terms change, we publish a new version and ask you to accept it again before you continue. We record the version you accepted and when.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: This page explains what data ESTAFET stores, what for, and what you can do with it.

s1.p: Account: name, email address, and university or faculty if you give them. Projects: the details you enter and the files you upload. Access and requests: who holds access to which project, and the messages in requests. Reports and appeals. Notifications. A record of which version of the terms and policies you accepted, and when. Your notification email setting and the language of your emails. The email queue keeps the kind of message and the content of the notification, not your email address.

s2.p: Data is kept in the database and file storage service ESTAFET uses (Supabase). Project files sit in private storage and are opened only through short-lived links after a permission check. Email is sent through the email provider ESTAFET uses; that provider receives your email address, your name and the content of the message. The account confirmation email is sent by Supabase through the same provider.

s3.p: If you ask for an AI draft, the text of the files you choose is sent to the AI provider ESTAFET is configured to use. Every team member must agree first. Source code is not sent apart from the README and package manifests. You can decline: choose “Fill in by hand without AI” and nothing is sent.

s4.p: The identity of a reporter is never shown to the project owners. Reports from guests store only a hashed form of the network address to limit abuse, not the address itself.

s5.p: We use only essential cookies: your sign-in session and your language choice. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.

s6.p: You can download a copy of your data (JSON) and ask for your account to be deleted from the Account privacy page. Deletion has a 30 day waiting period. After it, your profile becomes “Pengguna lama” (former user). Published projects stay without your name so teams that continued them keep a correct attribution line, unless you unpublish them before the waiting period ends.

s7.p: Account data is kept while your account exists. Records of accepted terms, lineage entries and moderation audit entries are kept longer because they serve as evidence. Technical logs do not contain file contents or personal data.

s8.p: Questions about personal data? See the Contact page.

guidelines.title: Community Guidelines
guidelines.lead: The ESTAFET team uses these rules to judge reports. They keep shared projects honest, safe and owned by people who have the right to share them.

s1.p: Do not share work that is not yours or that you may not share, such as other people's reports, closed-license code or paid material.

s2.p: Do not share other people's personal data without permission: ID numbers, addresses, private contacts, grades or research participant data.

s3.p: Do not write summaries, results or evidence you know are untrue. Show what was really finished and what was not.

s4.p: No content that harasses, threatens, spreads hatred, or is unfit for an academic setting.

s5.p: Do not claim to own or to have been on the team of a project that is not yours.

s6.p: Do not upload files that contain malware, passwords, secret keys or anything designed to cause harm.

s7.p: Do not use ESTAFET for advertising, unrelated links or pointless mass uploads.

s8.p: The team reads every report. If several different reporters report something serious (copyright, personal data, harmful files), the project is held for review. A hold is not a finding that a rule was broken. Every decision (dismiss, hold, hide, remove, restore) has a written reason. Owners receive the reason and can appeal once. Reporters' identities are never shown to owners.

attribution.title: Attribution Agreement
attribution.lead: Everyone who takes access to a project's files accepts this agreement. It is a simple template for student projects.

s1.p: You credit the original owners by name in any submission, paper or product page that builds on this project. The owners state they have the right to share the files. Ownership of the original work stays with its owners, and your new work belongs to you. ESTAFET records the handover in the lineage.

s2.p: Every project has a credit line you can copy from the project room, with the title, the owners' names and the lineage code.

s3.p: The agreement has a version number. Your acceptance is recorded with its version. If a new version is published, projects you already took stay under the version you accepted.

s4.p: The owners or the ESTAFET team can revoke your access with a written reason. The attribution duty stays for work you already made with help from that project.

s5.p: This is a simple template for student projects and is not legal advice. Check your university's rules for shared work.

row.effect: {label} changes from {from} to {to}. It applies immediately without a redeploy, and the before and after values are written to the audit log.

emails.title: Email log
emails.intro: Product emails from the outbox. Never shows addresses or message text, only the template, status, attempts and short error codes.
emails.skippedHint: The person turned notification emails off
emails.providerBanner: EMAIL_PROVIDER is {provider}: emails are queued but no real email is delivered.
emails.kindEssential: Essential: sent even when the person turned notification emails off
emails.resendEffect: Puts this email back in the queue with 5 new attempts. The next run of the email job sends it to the address the account has now.
emails.resendReason: Why do you send it again? (saved in the audit log)
emails.resent: Queued again. It goes out with the next email run.
emails.resendOnlyEssential: Only essential emails can be sent again. The in-app notification is still there.
emails.search: Search template, recipient or error code
emails.caption: Email outbox
emails.emptyText: Emails appear after the scheduled email job turns notifications into outbox rows.
emails.footnote: Bounces are not tracked: no provider webhook is connected, so "sent" means the provider accepted the email, not that it reached the inbox. Sent and skipped rows are removed after 90 days.

err.no_address: The account has no email address any more (for example, it was deleted).
err.unknown_template: The sender does not know this template. This is a bug: report it to the developers.
err.resend: Resend refused the email. The number is the HTTP status from Resend.
err.smtp: The SMTP server refused the email or could not be reached.
err.other: An unexpected error while sending. Check the server logs for email.failed.

common.fallbackLink: If the button does not work, copy this address into your browser: {url}
common.footerEssential: This email is about the safety of your account or project, so it is sent even if you turned notification emails off.
common.footerPrefs: You get this email because notification emails are on. You can turn them off in your account settings:

new_request.subject: New request for {title}
new_request.detail: Read their plan, then approve, decline or ask a question. A request with no answer expires.

approved.subject: Your request for {title} was approved
approved.intro: The owners approved your request to continue {title}.
approved.detail: Next step: accept the attribution agreement on your dashboard so the private files open.

declined.subject: Your request for {title} was declined
declined.intro: The owners could not accept your request for {title} right now.
declined.detail: You can ask again after the waiting period shown on the project page.

creator.subject: The owners of {title} accepted the attribution agreement
creator.intro: The owners of {title} accepted the attribution agreement.
creator.detail: If you have not accepted it yet, do it on your dashboard so the private files open.

adopter.subject: The continuing team accepted the attribution agreement for {title}
adopter.intro: The continuing team accepted the attribution agreement for {title}.
adopter.detail: If you have not accepted it yet, do it on your dashboard.

hold.subject: {title} is being held for review
hold.intro: The ESTAFET team is holding {title} for now while it reviews incoming reports.

hide.subject: {title} was hidden from public pages
hide.intro: The ESTAFET team hid {title} from public pages.

remove.subject: {title} was removed from public view
remove.intro: The ESTAFET team removed {title} from public view.

restore.subject: {title} was restored
restore.intro: The ESTAFET team restored {title}. Your project is back on public pages.

moderation.reason: Reason: “{reason}”. Your data and any signed agreement are unchanged.
moderation.appeal: You can appeal from your dashboard.

accepted.subject: Your appeal for {title} was accepted
accepted.intro: The ESTAFET team accepted your appeal. The earlier decision about {title} was reversed.

rejected.subject: Your appeal for {title} was rejected
rejected.intro: The ESTAFET team reviewed your appeal and the earlier decision about {title} stands.

access_revoked.subject: Your access to {title} was revoked
access_revoked.intro: The owners revoked your access to the private files of {title}.
access_revoked.detail: The attribution duty for what you already used still applies.

team_invite.subject: You were invited to co-own {title}
team_invite.intro: You were invited to co-own the project {title}.
team_invite.detail: Accept or decline the invitation on your dashboard.

ownership_offer.subject: You were offered ownership of {title}
ownership_offer.intro: An owner offered you ownership of the project {title}.
ownership_offer.detail: Accept or decline the offer in the project settings. Nothing changes until you answer.

report_outcome.subject: Report {reference} was reviewed
report_outcome.resolved: The ESTAFET team followed up on your report {reference}.
report_outcome.dismissed: The ESTAFET team reviewed your report {reference} and found no reason to act.
report_outcome.detail: Thank you for helping keep ESTAFET safe. Your identity is never shown to the project owners.

admin_hold.subject: [Admin] Project held: {title}
admin_hold.intro: The project {title} was held and needs a review.

admin_hold_overdue.subject: [Admin] Hold past its review target: {title}
admin_hold_overdue.intro: The project {title} has been held past its review target.
admin_hold_overdue.detail: Decide: restore, hide or remove, with a written reason.

admin_appeal.subject: [Admin] New appeal for {title}
admin_appeal.intro: The owners of {title} appealed a moderation decision.
admin_appeal.detail: One appeal is open per decision. Review it and give an outcome.

styleguide.title: Styleguide
styleguide.lead: Every design token and shared component of ESTAFET in one place, to compare against the approved design.
styleguide.notice: This page is not in the navigation, is not indexed by search engines and does not exist in production.

colors.title: Colors
colors.lead: Tokens from src/styles/tokens.css. Use the token, never the raw hex value.

type.title: Typography
type.lead: Instrument Sans for headings and text, DM Mono for small labels and buttons, JetBrains Mono for code and file names.
type.heading: Where the project stopped
type.body: A new team should understand the objectives, the finished work and the verified next steps without digging through old chats.
type.secondary: Secondary text for hints and metadata.
type.label: Small mono label
type.code: File names use the code font.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.lead: Pills with mono labels. One primary action per screen. The sky row shows the variants made for the sky background.

badges.title: Badges and chips
badges.lead: Status language from the design: owner verified, sample data and the evidence check.

cards.title: Cards
cards.lead: Soft rounded cards (28 px). Pick the tone by meaning, not by taste.

tone.white: White card on a grey area

fields.title: Form fields
fields.lead: Every field has a visible label. Hints and errors are linked to the field for screen readers.
fields.title1Hint: Short and specific, up to 80 characters.
fields.emailError: This email address is incomplete. Check the part after @.
fields.check: I confirm that my team agrees to share this project.
fields.error: Could not save. Check the fields marked in red and try again.

stepper.title: Stepper
stepper.lead: Shows progress in a flow. The current step carries aria-current.
stepper.label: Example progress

interactive.title: Interactive components
interactive.lead: Built on Radix: they render in portals, trap focus, close with Escape and return focus to the trigger.
interactive.panelOne: The first panel. Use the arrow keys to move between tabs.
interactive.panelTwo: The second panel slides in when the tab changes.
interactive.dialogText: The public summary becomes visible on Explore. Your files stay private.
interactive.drawerText: The phone navigation uses this panel.
interactive.tooltipText: A short hint for a control or a value.
interactive.toastSaved: Saved. You can undo this for 10 seconds.

layers.title: Layers
layers.lead: The only allowed z-index values (CLAUDE.md 14.9). Overlays live in portals on these layers.

motion.title: Motion
motion.lead: Animate transform and opacity only. Reduced motion turns off floating, drifting and reveals.
